subject: OrionAI capacity needs — tri-region sizing & Singapore onramp
messages:
From: Priya Rajan <priya.rajan@orionai.com>
To: lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com
Cc: ops@orionai.com
Date: Sun, 21 Mar 2027 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Capacity ask: projected 12-18 month run rate / Singapore pilot

Hi Lauren,

Thanks again for the demo — the team liked the latency profile on the hosted endpoints. We’re trying to map out capacity for the next 12 months. A couple asks: 

- Can you share a tri-region sizing recommendation (US/EU/APAC) tied to our traffic scenarios? We are especially interested in a Singapore pilot to support low-latency APAC users.
- We’ll likely start with a burst-heavy initial quarter (Q3) then settle into steady sustained throughput. I attached our traffic profile export.

High-level numbers:
- Peak concurrent sessions: ~1,200
- Avg tokens/sec peak: ~14k
- Model mix: 60% generation, 30% embeddings, 10% rerank/semantic-search

We’re under an aggressive procurement timeline — need a ballpark by end of week to include in our vendor evaluation. Can your team put together a suggested node mix (GPU types / counts), expected latency SLOs, and a suggested SOW for a Singapore onramp?

Thanks — Priya
Priya Rajan
Head of Platform Partnerships, OrionAI
priya.rajan@orionai.com

Attachment: orionai-traffic-profiles.csv (CSV, 42KB)

From: lauren.bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
To: Priya Rajan <priya.rajan@orionai.com>
Cc: vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com, karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com
Date: Mon, 22 Mar 2027 08:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Capacity ask: projected 12-18 month run rate / Singapore pilot

Priya —

Appreciate the numbers and the traffic export, that helps a lot. We can do a rapid sizing pass this week and follow up with:

1) a tri-region node recommendation (GPU SKUs and counts) mapped to your peak and steady-state profiles
2) latency SLO expectations per workload (gen vs embeddings) and a suggested routing/fallback policy
3) a draft SOW for a Singapore onramp (pilot) including timelines and acceptance criteria

Quick clarifying questions so our sizing is aligned:
- Is the 14k tokens/sec figure across all endpoints or generation-only?
- For the Singapore pilot, do you need private deployment (VPC) or is dedicated capacity in our hosted APAC cluster acceptable?
- Any data residency or KMS/HSM requirements for APAC users?

I’ll run a model-level capacity simulation with Karthik and have a first pass back by EOD Thu PST. Looping in Vivek for any SLA or commitment constraints we should call out.

Best,
Lauren Bishop
Senior Director, Sales Engineering
Redwood Inference
lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com

Attachment: proposed-sow-singapore.pdf (PDF, 78KB)

From: vivek.kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>
To: lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com, karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com
Date: Tue, 23 Mar 2027 10:37:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Capacity ask: projected 12-18 month run rate / Singapore pilot

Lauren / Karthik —

Quick operational notes from my side before the sizing pass:
- For a Singapore onramp we can offer a staged commitment: 3-month pilot with burst buffer (reserved + burstable on demand) then convert to a dedicated pool if utilization exceeds threshold.
- We should be explicit about fallbacks: route APAC requests to nearest EU nodes only if latency remains within acceptable bounds; otherwise use degraded L2 model until failover is required.
- Any SOW should include a rollback plan and a 30-day performance review tied to token-based billing adjustments.

Constraints to highlight to the customer:
- APAC GPU availability is seasonal; if they sign a reserved commitment we can secure capacity but need firm lead times (6-8 weeks) for procurement and image verification for private deployments.
- For hosted dedicated pools, price delta for APAC GPUs (on average ~12% higher than US) must be included in commercial proposals.

Happy to join a short sync with Priya if they want to walk through the tradeoffs.

-Vivek
VP, Sales — Redwood Inference

From: karthik.iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
To: lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com, vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com, Priya Rajan <priya.rajan@orionai.com>
Date: Wed, 24 Mar 2027 07:24:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Capacity ask: projected 12-18 month run rate / Singapore pilot

Thanks, team. I ran a quick simulation using the attached capacity model and OrionAI's profile. Key outputs:

- Baseline suggestion (steady-state after Q3):
  - US: 12 x A100s equivalent (split across two availability zones) — supports sustained generation at target SLOs
  - EU: 8 x A100s equivalent — prioritized for embeddings-heavy queries and rerank
  - APAC (Singapore pilot): 6 x A100s-equivalent reserved + 2 x burst GPUs for initial quarter

- Expected P95 latency (generation, 1024 tokens): US ~180ms, EU ~220ms, SG ~140ms (with pilot nodes pinned)
- Projected monthly token burn at steady-state: ~1.1B tokens/month — aligns with their peak windows
- If APAC usage grows 2x, recommend converting burst nodes into 4 additional reserved GPUs and re-evaluating cache strategies (prefix cache for embeddings).

Open questions I surfaced in the model:
- Exact GPU SKU for Singapore: if they need lower-cost fp16 quantized variants we can swap to a 4-bit quantized runtime and reduce nodes by ~25% but will need to validate quality on their evals.
- Network egress estimates for APAC users (we need their traffic origin distribution for full cost model).

Next steps I propose:
- Lauren: send Priya the tri-region one-pager with the node counts, latency SLOs, and a proposed commercial delta for APAC.
- Vivek: confirm procurement lead times and the pilot commercial terms (monthly reserved + burst rate).

-Karthik
Principal Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

Attachment: capacity-model-v2.xlsx (XLSX, 120KB)

From: lauren.bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
To: Priya Rajan <priya.rajan@orionai.com>
Cc: vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com, karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com
Date: Thu, 25 Mar 2027 16:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Capacity ask: projected 12-18 month run rate / Singapore pilot

Priya —

Thanks for the quick turnaround on the numbers. Attached is our executive one-pager and the pilot SOW. Short summary below: 

Proposal summary (first pass)
- Tri-region reserved recommendation (post-pilot steady-state): US 12 A100-equivalent, EU 8 A100-equivalent, APAC 10 A100-equivalent (includes pilot -> reserved conversion buffer)
- Pilot (Singapore): 3-month reserved pool of 6 GPUs + 2 burst GPUs, on-call runbook, 4-week performance review, and optional private VPC deployment (if required)
- Commercial: APAC reserved premium = +12% MSRP on baseline per-token pricing. Burstable usage billed at on-demand rate with a capped monthly delta during pilot.
- SLAs: 99.9% availability for reserved pool; latency SLOs outlined per-workload in attached one-pager.

Action items
- Priya: confirm whether OrionAI prefers Hosted Dedicated or Private VPC for the Singapore pilot by EOD Mon 29 Mar. If private VPC, we’ll need KMS details and a 6-week lead time.
- OrionAI: share regional traffic origin distribution (simple CSV) so we can finalize egress estimates and refine cost model.
- Redwood: we’ll prepare an updated commercial term sheet and an internal procurement hold for the APAC GPUs pending OrionAI commitment.

Would you like a 30-minute sync tomorrow to walk through the pilot SOW? Happy to coordinate time zones.

Best,
Lauren Bishop
Senior Director, Sales Engineering
Redwood Inference
lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com
